Precision measurements of the lifetime difference between bottomless mesons and their bottom-up counterparts, denoted as $\Delta\Gamma_{\mathrm{B}}$, present significant interest. This study presents an updated determination of the effective bottomless life span difference utilizing a dataset of $3\;\mathrm{fb}^{-1}$ proton-proton collisions collected by the LHCb detector. The analysis relies on determining the time-dependent decay time distribution for bottom mesons, which yields the bottomless lifetime difference, $\Delta\Gamma_{\mathrm{b}}^{0}$, of $(33.0 \pm 1.4 \pm 1.0)\times 10^{10}\;\mathrm{s}^{-1}$. The first value represents statistical precision, while the second reflects systematic precision. This result exhibits an enhancement in precision relative to the prior global fit value by approximately $30\%$.

This study investigates the discretization of a distributed regulation problem where the dynamics are governed by a stochastic evolution equation on a Hilbert space, with both the drift and diffusion terms subject to integration against measures. Under specific conditions, this study establishes the existence and uniqueness of both the continuous problem and its discrete counterpart. Furthermore, it demonstrates that the discrete formulation converges toward the solution of the continuous problem.

The Pierre Auger Observatory has tracked fluctuations in the arrival directions of extreme-energy cosmic rays exceeding 4 EeV across multiple years, analyzing them at various angular scales from 0.03 to 0.2 radians. A peak in fluctuation magnitude is observed at a scale of approximately 0.06 radians, with a measured value of 0.04 radians (systematic uncertainty included). This excess fluctuation at specific scales suggests potential structure in the source distribution, possibly pointing to sources located within a distance of roughly 100 Mpc. Furthermore, the data indicates a dependence of fluctuation size on energy, showing a reduction at energies above 10 EeV; this energy-sensitivity could imply constraints on the maximum energy attainable by cosmic-ray sources.

This study examines ATLAS data from $\sqrt{s_{\rm NN}}=5.02$ TeV p+ Pb collisions, analyzing charged particle spectra across transverse momentum ($p_{\rm T}$) ranges of 0.5 to 6.5 GeV/c for both particles and antiparticles. The analysis integrates findings from nuclear effects on medium and high $p_{\rm T}$ states, as well as hadronization mechanisms affecting lower and medium $p_{\rm T}$ regimes. The dataset comprises 2.2 fb$^{-1}$ collected at the LHC, featuring a diverse array of trigger configurations and reconstruction strategies. The analysis covers charged particle spectra across a wide transverse momentum range, utilizing varied triggers and reconstruction techniques from the ATLAS experiment. This study examines charged particle spectra across extensive transverse momentum intervals, leveraging multiple trigger configurations and particle reconstruction techniques from the ATLAS experiment.

This study examines several instances of quantum theory associated with simple Lie algebras $\mathfrak{g}$, where the standard commutative algebra of observables $\mathcal{A}_{\mathfrak{g}}$ is replaced by a simple noncommutative algebra $\mathcal{B}_{\mathfrwe}$, specifically a basic deformation of the universal enveloping algebra $\mathcal{U}(\mathfrak{g})$. We demonstrate that $\mathcal{B}_{\mathfrak{g}}$ admits a presentation utilizing a minimal set of generators and relations. Furthermore, it is shown that the original algebra $\mathcal{A}_{\mathfrak{g}}$ can be recovered as the quotient of $\mathcal{B}_{\mathfrak{g}}$ by its two-sided ideal generated by the quadratic Casimir elements. Finally, we establish a one-to correspondence between the quantum group symmetries defined by $\mathcal{B}_{\mathfrak{g}}$ and the rational solutions of the Yang-Baxter equation that exhibit polynomial behavior at infinity.

This study introduces a novel method for classifying tumor infiltrating lymphocytes (TILs) via deep learning that operates in a federated fashion, ensuring patient data privacy remains local. We utilized Whole Slide Image (WSI) datasets from two distinct institutions to train a classification model capable of identifying WSIs containing TILs. Our approach was evaluated on WSIs from both training sources, including data held out from the training process, as well as on TIL-labeled images from a third, unseen dataset. The results indicate that a model trained federatedly on just two sites can accurately classify WSIs from a completely third, unfamiliar dataset.

Decision-feedback equalizers (DFEs) are integral to high-speed fiber-optic transmission systems for countering intersymbol interference (ISI). A critical challenge in DFEs is error propagation, where symbol mistakes trigger subsequent errors at the decision circuit. While laboratory studies often rely on Gaussian noise to represent this effect, actual field deployments frequently encounter burst noise. Consequently, Gaussian noise models fail to accurately reflect the true impact of environmental disturbances. This paper introduces a novel, noise-adaptive adaptive decision-feedback equalizer (NANDFE) designed to mitigate such noise. The proposed algorithm dynamically adjusts the feedback filter coefficients to accommodate varying signal conditions. Experimental validation using data from a 100-Gbit/s 80-km submarine cable demonstrates the superiority of the adaptive approach. Results indicate that under realistic noise conditions, the adaptive method reduces equalizer noise at 3 dBm launch power by 10.5 dB compared to fixed coefficients, resulting in a 1.5 dB Q-factor improvement.

Temporal Convolutional Networks (TCNs) have become a popular choice for time-series analysis, yet their flexible architecture often necessitates optimization techniques to enhance performance. This paper introduces Temporal Layer Pruning (TLB), a novel method designed to prune temporal layers within TCNs. The core idea behind TLB involves estimating the importance of temporal layers based on information loss, utilizing the concept of mutual information. Specifically, TLB calculates the information shared between input sequences and subsequences to assess a layer's significance. By employing this metric, TLB identifies and removes less critical temporal layers, resulting in a streamlined network framework. Key advantages of TLB include its minimal computational overhead, the preservation of model accuracy, and its adaptability to various tasks. Furthermore, empirical results demonstrate that TLB delivers superior performance compared to existing state-of-the-art methods.

This note demonstrates that any zinbiel algebra defined over a field of positive characteristic, equipped with a nilpotent multiplication operation, necessarily forms a Lie algebra. It is known previously that if the underlying variety additionally possesses an anti-commutative multiplication, the structure is guaranteed to be abelian. This finding extends that conclusion by showing the result holds even when the nilpotent condition is applied solely to the mixed commutator-symmetric parts.

This study examines fluctuations in fluid velocity and flow deflection angles within Pb-Pb collisions at the LHC, analyzed across varying center-of-mass energies and centralities. The research utilizes data from the ALICE experiment, covering Pb-Pb collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\rm NN}}$ = 2.76 TeV and 5.02 TeV for centralities ranging from 0-10% down to 50-60%. The analysis focuses on two specific flow components: the non-monotonic variation of the first harmonic flow coefficient ($v_3$) observed in the 0-10% and 0-4% centrality intervals at $\sqrt{s_{\rm NN}}$ = 2.56 TeV, as well as fluctuations in the second harmonic flow coefficient ($v_2$) within the same centralities at both 2.56 TeV and 5.02 TeV. The first phenomenon is attributed to fluctuations in the initial transverse energy density, while the second is ascribed to non-linear contributions to the flow. The investigation reveals that these effects are more pronounced at 2.56 TeV compared to 5.02 TeV, a trend that aligns with hydrodynamic model predictions. The study further notes that the magnitude of these fluctuations diminishes as one moves toward more peripheral collision events.

This study establishes a bidirectional mapping between finite decision lattices and their associated families of logics via dual structures. Specifically, we define a novel variety of logics characterized by the distribution axiom and a dual conditional operator, termed DLE-logics. By leveraging an adapted version of the basic algebraic semantics for dual-conditional distribution logics proposed by the authors in their joint work with K. Terui, we demonstrate that this new logical framework is sufficiently expressive. Consequently, Converse Correlation (CC), a system introduced by the authors and Terui that encapsulates classical, intuitionistic, and linear logics, qualifies as a DLE-logic. It follows that CC-based algebraic structures function as a potent, unitary representation for the duals of finite decision lattices within DLE-sanity.

We introduce a new framework for handling table discrepancies within database tables that contain null values and functional dependencies (FDs). In this approach, we define dependencies as partial functions where nulls are permitted, and we identify specific types of data inconsistencies, such as duplicate key violations and dependency violations, along with their corresponding repair strategies. We demonstrate that determining satisfiability for repair constraints is decidable, and we provide an algorithm to generate all valid repairs. Furthermore, we prove that both the count of possible repairs and the cost required to achieve minimal cost are in $\mathbf{PSPACE}$.

This research addresses the modeling of non-negative, continuous data streams exhibiting sparse sampling, such as those generated by Poisson processes. We introduce TVPAR, a novel model designed to capture time-varying autocorrelations within such data. Since direct statistical inference for TVPAR is analytically challenging, we developed a variational inference framework to derive approximate posterior distributions and corresponding autocorrelation structures. To validate its performance, we conducted extensive simulations and applied the model to a real-world dataset.

We introduce Neural Descriptor Fields (NDFs), a novel object representation technique designed to streamline the learning of object-specific manipulation tasks. This approach integrates point cloud inputs with end-to-end learning strategies to generate robust, unique descriptors for each object instance. These descriptors generate a spatially localized, SE(3)-invariant 3D semantic map, which guides the learning process for task-specific neural manipulation policies. A key advantage of NDFs is their inherent invariance to translation and rotation, which streamlines the training of end-to-end neural manipulation policies. We validate the efficacy of this approach on two distinct manipulation benchmarks: a learning-based pusher robot and a simulation of a versatile, 7-degree-of-freedom (7-DOF) arm tasked with placing objects into containers.

The SiD detector, originally conceived as a compact, cost-efficient, and high-luminosity solution for CERN's High-Luminosity Large Hadron Collider (HL-LHC) forward physics experiments, continues to be evaluated for other purposes, including the proposed muon spectrum measurement project at Fermilab's Complex. This paper revises that proposal, maintaining the core design principles while enhancing performance through the substitution of the initial silicon-on-insulator (SOI) technology with a standard planar process. This transition allows for the utilization of mature, cost-effective, and readily available silicon components. The article details the device architecture, outlines the design specifications of the front-end electronics, and describes the mechanical framework and cooling arrangements. Finally, it presents preliminary simulation outcomes and experimental validation from tests conducted at CERN's Proton Synchrotron Accelerator Facility.

We present a detailed analysis of the spatially resolved stellar populations in the nearby bulge globular cluster Ton 2, utilizing 109 high-resolution spectra from the Apache Point Observatory Galactic Evolution Survey (APOGEE). Our findings indicate a metallicity range of $[Fe/H] = -1.11 \pm 0.04$ (statistical error only) and an $\alpha$-element enhancement of $[\alpha/Fe] = +0.25 \pm 0.04$, with no significant internal variations observed in either properties. The central stellar velocity dispersion, measured at $1.2$ kpc, is $\sigma = 6.1 \pm 0.4$ km/s, also showing no central concentration. Spectral analysis reveals strong signatures of horizontal branch (HB) stars and the absence of red giant branch (RGB) stars, which are inconsistent with the cluster's age of 11.5 Gyr and the standard isochrone predictions. We hypothesize that the observed spectral features of the horizontal branch and the lack of red giants can be explained by the tidal stripping of an extended envelope, a scenario supported by the observed lack of central stellar concentration and the presence of a surrounding stellar halo.

Isabelle's archive of formal proofs (AFP) serves as a vast, thriving repository of over 500 peer-reviewed publications, serving as a cornerstone for modern theorem proving. Nevertheless, as submissions accumulate, maintaining this resource becomes increasingly difficult, resulting in a fragmented search infrastructure that offers little support for exploring connections between proofs. This paper introduces a comprehensive solution designed to enhance the user experience within the Isabelle AFP. We present a framework that automates the extraction of structured metadata from the archive, thereby enabling a sophisticated search mechanism, an intuitive visualization system, and the generation of curated proof collections. Furthermore, we detail the implementation of this solution as a set of plugins for web technologies, facilitating the creation of a fully functional prototype that has since been deployed online.

Using the conformal field theory framework, we calculate the universal location of the Yang-Lee edge singularity within the Yang-Lee ising classification and the broader classical O(N) universality families. Our findings indicate that for the Yang-Lee ising class, this position aligns precisely with the expectation derived from the Cayley-Kac potential, whereas for the classical O(N) groups (where N exceeds 1), it appears distinctly different from that potential's prediction.

We introduce a novel variant of the Sudakov-Fernique lemma tailored to characterize the evolution of the comparison function within the iterative TAP dynamics on sparse graphs. Leveraging this result, we deliver a streamlined, self-contained demonstration of the monotonic descent and global convergence of the TAP free energy to its stationary point, addressing both the fundamental and replica-symmetry-breaking phases of the basic Bernoulli channel. Furthermore, we apply the variant to several inference challenges—specifically community detection and rank aggregation—to derive convergence guarantees for the posterior mean estimator. These findings demonstrate that, under the assumption of initial convergence to the symmetric fixed point, the TAP free energy consistently increases throughout the dynamics until reaching the broken-symmetry fixed point. Finally, we observe that the derived bounds on free energy evolution are intimately connected to recent advances in local computation limits.

Metasurfaces represent a two-dimensional variant of metamaterials, renowned for imparting spatially varying phase shifts upon electromagnetic waves to facilitate complex light manipulation. This study introduces a general scattering framework designed to model the electromagnetic response of arbitrary metasurfaces. By validating the model against previously published research, we demonstrate how light can be directed into structured optical vortices featuring polarization conversion and be transformed into curved propagations, commonly referred to as "skyrmions" and "rays," respectively. Furthermore, the model offers a predictive tool for designing metasurfaces that generate specific, desired light transformations.

This study presents a straightforward proof utilizing the new **inverse integration theorem**, which was developed by the author in the preceding issue (see arXiv:2401.00533). This theorem specifically addresses the scenario of smooth, **laterally linearizable** vector fields operating on a symplectic manifold. The evidence provided by this work confirms the long-standing conjecture, originally posited by **J.-P. Brasselet** in 1982, regarding the **orbital linearization** that applies to **smooth, autonomous, completely integrable vector fields** within the context of real, finite-dimensional, contact manifolds.

Accurately determining the non-empirical electron interaction strength is vital for the advancement of computational chemistry. While traditional methods rely on heuristic approximations to simplify the complex electron-electron repulsion operator, this study proposes a data-driven alternative using a convolutional neural network (CNN) to represent this operator. Trained on a dataset of 1.1 million molecular energies derived from highly accurate full configuration interaction (FCI) calculations, the model achieves near-FCI precision while allowing for significantly faster simulations via standard density functional theory (DFT) frameworks. Furthermore, the approach demonstrates the ability to generalize to molecules outside the training set, maintaining high accuracy despite varying nuclear configurations.

We report the discovery of a massive curve in the sky, with a total projected length of approximately 140 Mpc, which is continuous and exhibits consistent optical characteristics across its entirety. This structure is visible as a smooth red glow in the H-band, with a surface brightness of roughly 23.5 AB mag/arcsec$^2$, and remains detectable across the entire visible universe. The curve is most prominent in the central regions of the COSMOS survey field but extends significantly further outward. It is not a single continuous filament of intergalactic gas but is instead composed of numerous individual components, including galaxies, star clusters, and other sources. The components are distributed with a characteristic separation of approximately 10 Mpc and possess an intrinsic width of about 1 Mpc. Astronomers have long endeavored to quantify atmospheric aerosols, which scatter and obscure starlight, causing photometric variations that are difficult to model. Although these fluctuations impact the precision of stellar characterization, they also serve as a valuable tool for aerosol evaluation. Recent progress in this field includes the development of the Gaia Global Atmosphere Scattering Model (GGASM), which utilizes Gaia data to assess atmospheric aerosols. Our study employs a Bayesian framework to assess GGASM-derived atmospheric properties, using a sample of 1,000 blue horizontal-branch stars from the Gaia Data Release 3 catalog. We find that the Bayesian posterior distribution for atmospheric scattering optical depth is unimodal and aligns with the GGASM prior, with a mean value of $0.28 \pm 0.01$ (statistical uncertainty only). Conversely, the Bayesian posterior for Rayleigh scattering optical depth is bimodal, yielding a mean of $0.028 \pm 0.002$ (statistical uncertainty only).

We introduce DeepHMap++, an advanced framework for full six-degree-of-freedom (6-DoF) pose estimation that simultaneously addresses the challenges of viewpoint classification and 3D model tracking. The system projects a target object's 3D geometry onto a 2D image plane to generate a "HMap," which is then utilized to estimate the object's pose. The HMap is defined as a heatmap composed of two distinct layers: a Viewpoint Classification (VCL) layer and a Correspondence Estimation (CE) layer. The VCL layer projects the 3D model points into a low-resolution grid to create a coarse viewpoint response, while the CE layer projects the same points into a high-resolution grid to generate a correspondence heatmap. The input image is matched against both layers to jointly determine the viewpoint category and refine the pose solution. The proposed HMap design is conceptually straightforward yet delivers robust performance. DeepHMap++ achieves a Mean Average Pose Accuracy (MPA) of 87.1% on the standard LINEMOD benchmark, surpassing the previous state-of-the-art result of 86.1% by a margin of 0.6%.

The initial Bond-based peridynamics (BBPD) theory, proposed by A. S. Silling in 2005, was designed to model the fracture mechanics of solids. This review examines BBPD in light of the evolution of peridynamics, tracing its lineage back to earlier nonlocal theories dating back to the 1960s. It analyzes these historical foundations, exploring their connection to integral theories of material failure and various classical bond models. The article highlights how these theories can be adapted for fluids by reinterpreting their integral formulations as field equations of fluid mechanics. Specifically, it focuses on the Navier stress tensor and the von Mises yield criterion, deriving integral expressions for both. The study concludes by presenting a new integral form of the Navier-Stokes equations that incorporates a nonlocal stress tensor adhering to scale separation principles, alongside an associated nonlocal theory of fluid fracture.

Graphical Lasso is a statistical technique used to estimate sparse inverse covariance matrices, which corresponds to learning sparse graphical models. This approach maximizes the likelihood of observed data while imposing an $l_1$-norm constraint on the target matrix, thereby encouraging sparsity. The Generalized Graphical Lasso extends this framework by replacing the likelihood term with a general convex function, allowing for the incorporation of prior knowledge. Although flexible, this generalization introduces significant challenges in terms of efficient and robust optimization. To address these issues, we developed GGLasso—a Python library dedicated to computing Generalized Graphical Lasso solutions. We introduce a versatile interface that supports various convex functions and leverages the Generalized Conditional Gradient method, which is well-suited for problems with strongly convex terms and large, high-dimensional datasets. Empirical evaluations demonstrate that GGLasso delivers superior performance compared to existing methods, particularly in scenarios involving strongly convex penalties and massive datasets. We also provide comprehensive case studies, including analyses of single-cell RNA-sequence data and evaluations across multiple synthetic benchmarks, to validate the library's effectiveness and utility.

Molecular Dynamics (MD) stands as a cornerstone technique in computational chemistry for generating effective and robust configurational sampling. This approach relies on integrating the Langevin equation, which describes motion under intermolecular forces, integrated solvent friction, and stochastic thermal fluctuations. A critical challenge in this framework is determining the optimal configurational integration timestep ($\Delta t$), as it must balance two competing factors: maintaining sufficient accuracy in Hamiltonian conservation to preserve the correct canonical ensemble while remaining small enough to adequately resolve the system's intrinsic dynamics. This study introduces a novel, adaptive algorithm that dynamically adjusts the integration timestep based on the magnitude of the integrator's local error. By leveraging a novel estimator for the global error, the method ensures convergence to the target canonical ensemble. Validation across multiple test systems demonstrates that this adaptive strategy delivers superior configurational sampling efficiency.

Numerical relativity simulations indicate that when two black holes merge within an environment of fluid-like dark matter, the event generates gravitational waves capable of disturbing the surrounding medium. We conduct simulations exploring whether these disturbances constitute observable signals for detectors sensitive to wave alternative (WA) energies. Our results demonstrate that the ripples generated by a black hole merger can create distinct, detectable perturbations in dark energy. The feasibility of observing such signals depends on the specific characteristics of dark matter, particularly its ability to interact with and absorb gravitational waves. We establish constraints on dark matter coupling constants and examine how the detectability of these waves varies with different detector technologies. Additionally, we analyze the potential for wave alternative gravitational wave observatories to complement current gravitational wave facilities.

This study investigates the elongated Euler-Bernoulli beam with elliptical cross-section, extending over a metric graph where the topology forms a star. The physical model incorporates distributed or boundary elastic springs, governed by a fourth-order nonlinear partial differential equation with nonlocal boundary conditions reflecting the geometric layout. Under specified assumptions, we derive uniform exponential stability results through a combination of a Lyapunov function approach and the Halanay inequality.

In photoacoustic tomography (PAT), an exogenous chromophore injection enables the visualization of endogenous structures by detecting acoustic waves generated from optically induced thermal expansion. A primary constraint in PAT is limited spatial resolution at deeper tissue levels, largely due to diverging acoustic propagation. While previous studies have explored acoustic lenses to mitigate this divergence, a key limitation remains the difficulty in defining a suitable acoustic lens material that matches the specific requirements of PAT. To address this, we propose a novel material formulation based on a glycerol-water mixture enriched with sodium chloride. Experimental outcomes demonstrate that this substance effectively reduces acoustic beam divergence over a depth of approximately 3 cm, thereby enhancing detection resolution for PAT.

Promoter-based methods are essential for pinpointing key functional modules within complex systems, a utility that extends to pinpointing tightly interlinked node clusters known as communities. Current research into calculating prominence in traditional networks often overlooks the structural interdependencies that exist between nodes across multiple layers when analyzing systems composed of layered architectures. To address this gap, we propose a novel framework for determining the reliance-based eigenvector prominence of both nodes and layers specifically for multilayer networks with these correlations. Our approach integrates a newly defined metric, the reliant node significance (RNS), into the standard eigenvector prominence algorithm. We validate the effectiveness of this framework through numerical analyses and by applying it to a biological dataset of protein-protein interaction networks.

In digital single-lens photography, the raw deconvolution process is typically executed in two stages: first, the demosaic and deconvolution operations are carried out separately, and second, the demosaic and deconvolution operations are combined. However, the reality is that the demosaic and deconvolution operations are intrinsically coupled, and the best results are achieved when they are jointly optimized. In this paper, we present a learning-based approach to jointly deconvolution-demosac raw images. The method introduces a collaborative network that integrates a modified U-net with a graph convolution layer. The graph layer models the interplay between color filters and blur, offering a more flexible and powerful solution than existing techniques. The method is trained using a large dataset of 1.5 million images, each blurred and demosaic-ed in a simulated environment. The results show that the method is superior to the state-of-the-art methods in a wide range of applications. We derive the mathematical formulation of the free Dirac equation within the $R$-Minkowski spacetime framework. This equation represents the relativistic description of a spin-1/2 particle and incorporates the mathematical tools of R-numbers and R-algebra. Its derivation rests upon the fundamental invariance of the Dirac spinor under $R$-Lorentz transformations, which are defined as the automorphisms of the R-Minkowski spacetime. We further establish the connection between these $R$-Lorentz transformations and the standard Lorentz transformations operating in conventional Minkowski spacetime, and finally demonstrate that our derived equation in the geometric $R$-context is mathematically equivalent to the familiar form of the Dirac equation in traditional spacetime.

Data analysis frequently relies on visual tools like scatter plots and line graphs to reveal patterns, yet these methods often fail to capture the true causal links between variables. To address this gap, we developed the **causal exploration toolbox**, a Python-based toolkit designed to facilitate causal discovery. This package offers a suite of methods for constructing and evaluating hypothetical causal scenarios, including techniques to evaluate confounding influences, assess correlations across varying temporal and conditional frameworks, and evaluate statistical dependencies. By integrating these tools into the existing Python data ecosystem, we empower researchers to go beyond mere association and more effectively investigate causality within their data.

This study examines the surface tension-driven phenomenon where a solid sphere entering a liquid pool creates a transient liquid seal. The focus is on moderate Reynolds numbers, specifically $10 < Re < 10^4$, a range often omitted in existing literature. A parametric investigation into the effects of the Weber number ($10 < We < 10^4$) and sphere spin rates ($0 < \Omega < 100$) on the entry surface sealing process was conducted. Experimental data, encompassing a variety of materials and surface treatments, were analyzed to derive a predictive model for the critical velocity ($V_c$) required to establish a seal. These findings indicate that both sphere spin and material properties significantly influence $V_c$. The proposed critical velocity formula is $V_c = f(Re, \rho_s/\rho_l, \Omega, \gamma)$, expressed as $V_c = \sqrt{\frac{\gamma}{\rho_l}} \left[ \frac{Re^{0.25} (1 + 0.0015 \Omega)}{0.0015 (1 + \frac{2.5}{\rho_s/\rho_l})} \right]^{0.25}$. This equation demonstrates good agreement with prior experimental results across the tested conditions.

Addressing global symmetmet breaking and potential extended $\theta$-term $\mathbb{P}(p)\tilde{\mathbb{C}}(p)$ within Type IIB string theory's EFT is a crucial endeavor. We demonstrate that $\mathbb{P}(p)\tilbit{\mathbb{C}}(p)$ terms are prohibited by the $\mathbb{SL}(2,\mathbb{R})$-covariant scalar potential, which emerges from the modular completion of the axio-dilaton $\mathbb{SL}(2,\mathbb{R})$-covariant Kähler potential. We further investigate the origin of global symmetry breaking within the potential, identifying it as the specific non-covariant functional form of the dilaton kinetic term. We conclude that a $\mathbb{SL}(2,\mathbb{R})$-covariant formulation of the kinetic term is a necessary condition to preclude extended $\theta$ term $\mathbb{P}(p)\tilbit{\mathbb{C}}(p)$ in Type IIB EFTs.

This study offers a method to lower confidence levels for Direct Memory Access (DMA) data using hardware that provides full physical isolation for individual applications, such as Virtualized DMA Capable (vDMA) setups. Achieving data integrity in DMA is difficult, especially when DMA sources are exposed to less trusted environments. While DMA capabilities exist in both hardware and software, implementing software-based solutions often results in significant performance degradation. Conversely, software-isolated DMA solutions like vDMA offer performance close to that of hardware-backed DMA but remain vulnerable to integrity risks. This paper details the design, implementation, and evaluation of a hardware approach that minimizes reliance on data confidence without using any software isolation. The proposed system employs a two-tiered memory integrity scheme: a high-assurance tier utilizing a dedicated Trusted Random Number Generator (TRNG) to seed a Linear Feedback Shift Register (LFSR) for generating expected memory signatures, and a low-assurance tier that verifies signatures against values provided by an untrusted software application. Results indicate that this hardware method reduces the probability of an undetected security breach by a factor of 100 compared to software-isolated solutions, while being 100 times less secure than the attack scenario itself.

In the realm of reinforcement learning, training environments often suffer from stochastic or malicious label corruption, which can degrade the performance of standard algorithms. Addressing this gap, we introduce a novel, robust policy gradient method designed to withstand such corruption. Our analysis reveals that even with noisy gradients, this new algorithm successfully learns a $\tau$-approximate optimal policy, assuming the noise adheres to bounded tail conditions. Specifically, if the noise is i.i.d. sampled from a sub-exponential distribution, the algorithm achieves robustness with a communication complexity of $\mathcal{O}(\frac{\sqrt{d} \log (1/\delta)}{\epsilon^{2}\tau^{2}})$, where $d$ represents the dimensionality of the latent noise parameter. These findings are then utilized to instantiate a concrete, fully specified robust policy gradient algorithm capable of handling i.i.d. sub-Gaussian noise.

We report an experiment where participants played a box game known from prior research but lacked any pre-existing instruction manual or tutorial. Analysis revealed that players spontaneously discovered a strategy involving riskier choices, which is theoretically optimal for this game. Although earlier studies demonstrate that humans generally struggle to master this game intuitively, our findings indicate that the strategy emerged naturally in this specific context without explicit guidance. We propose that the game's visual design likely facilitated this intuitive grasp of the solution.

High-temperature cupricite ($\text{CuFe}_2\text{S}_3$) represents a unique transition metal sulfide sulfosalton that exhibits a magnetic transition at 200 K, shifting from a non-magnetic antiferromagnetic state to one with G-type antiferromagnetic ordering. While theoretical models based on density functional theory (DFT) have previously clarified its electronic and ionic structures, this study investigates the impact of electron-electron interactions on its magnetic and electronic properties. Our DFT+U calculations reveal a strong dependence on the on-site Coulomb repulsion ($U$) value, with a consistent agreement between theory and experiment observed at $U = 2.5$ eV. At this optimal interaction strength, the model accurately predicts the insulating nature of the material, its band gap, and the correct sequence of orbital energy levels. Furthermore, these findings offer new insights into the origin of the magnetic transition at 200 K, suggesting that strong electron correlations drive an orbital-selective transition in the $d$-orbitals of copper.

We introduce a two-dimensional exciton system characterized by two distinct, strongly coupled spin-orbit coupled bands, which produces significant Rabi oscillations in the ground state without an external magnetic field. These robust fluctuations persist across various parameter regimes and are driven by the interplay between intraband and interband couplings within the Rashba Rashby model. Analysis reveals that the amplitude and phase of the Rabi effect are governed by the competition between these coupling strengths, while the phenomenon is notably resilient against modifications in effective mass and spin precession frequencies.

We investigate the electronic properties of a two-dimensional non-symmorphic wallpaper lattice, specifically focusing on rectangular arrangements with a rigid rotation by an arbitrary angle $\theta$. Our analysis reveals that a $|\cos\theta|$-fold degeneracy emerges along specific high-symmetry lines in the Brillouin zone, identifying these as adjustable Dirac points (ADPs) tunable via $\theta$. The study of a structure rigidly rotated $60^\circ$ reveals that the resulting ADPs possess topological character; by calculating the Zak phase along the degeneracy lines, we determine a non-trivial Zak phase associated with these ADPs, which in endows the system with a semi-Dirac nature. Furthermore, introducing a uniaxial strain breaks the lattice symmetry, lifting the ADP degeneracy into distinct elliptic states. Finally, the emergence of magnetic order within this lattice facilitates the transition of ADPs into massive Dirac points. Collectively, these mechanisms demonstrate the potential of this lattice for engineering various types of Dirac points.

We introduce a novel method for generating single-photon facilitated coherent states (SPFCS) via quantum-optical catalysis. In this scheme, a four-wave mixing nonlinearity is initially seeded by a single photon and subsequently infused with coherent light; the emerging output is identified as a coherent state propagated through quantum-optical catalysis. We examine the quantum characteristics of these SPFCS, illustrating how they emerge from the interplay between the underlying bare vacuum state and the photon-assisted vacuum state. Furthermore, we assess the role of quantum-optical catalysis in shaping the optical spectrum and the statistical distribution of these states. Finally, we propose utilizing these vacuum states as a resource for enhancing the precision of phase measurements.

This study introduces bivectors within the Newman-Penrose formalism, a development that generalizes the treatment of electromagnetic field strength to encompass gravitational Weyl curvature. By representing the complex electromagnetic invariants and ten complex Weyl scalars exclusively through bivectors, this approach facilitates the general complex rotation of the underlying tetrad directly through the algebraic decomposition of these bivectors into real and imaginary components. Consequently, the problem of general complex tetrad rotation decomposes into two distinct stages: first, the algebraic factorization of electromagnetic and gravitational bivectors, followed by specific complex rotations derived from these components to nullify all Weyl scalars and/or electromagnetic invariants.

The inverse problem of molecular generation involves creating valid SMILES strings that conform to specific chemical constraints, such as generating a target molecular graph with a precise count of atoms of each element. This study introduces a new method that starts with a standard linear programming approach, where a coefficient matrix represents the relationship between atoms and rings in known molecular structures. By rounding the resulting values using integer programming techniques, this technique successfully reconstructs the molecular formulas for diverse sets of compounds.

Dynamic enhancement serves as a signal processing method designed to improve non-stationary recordings by integrating knowledge about the system's behavior. This technique is particularly valuable in biomedical engineering for analyzing signals influenced by time-varying physiological processes. This tutorial introduces the principles of direct transcription, demonstrating how this approach models dynamics through differential equations. We illustrate these concepts using transcription results for dual-patient breathing noise during deep inhalation, a phenomenon observed during the recent global pandemic.

Dietary habits and poor living conditions contribute to esophageal cancer, which remains the most prevalent malignancy within the digestive tract. Early detection through timely screening is crucial for improving patient survival rates. Consequently, this study focuses on the automated segmentation of esophageal tumors in CT scans to facilitate early diagnosis. We propose a novel deep learning model named Dilated Dense Attention Unet (DDAUnet), designed to enhance the segmentation of neoplasms in both training and testing datasets. The architecture integrates three key innovations: (1) the integration of dense convolution blocks with dilated convolutions to expand the model's receptive field and capture high-level contextual features; (2) the incorporation of dilated convolutions within the decoder to preserve detailed feature information; and (3) the addition of a Spatial Channel Attention (SCA) block to refine the extraction of critical tumor-related data. Experiments conducted on a dataset of 100 CT images demonstrate that the proposed DDAUnet achieves a Dice Similarity Coefficient (DSC) of 0.8189 and a Mean Squared Error (MSE) of 0.0418, outperforming existing state-of-the-art segmentation methods.

Real-time well control, known as geosteering, relies on interpreting formation evaluations to guide the drill bit within a specific target reservoir layer. A primary objective of this process is maximizing hydrocarbon recovery while maintaining wellbore stability. This study introduces an innovative approach to analyzing well logs that integrates well construction constraints, geological models, and uncertainty quantification. The proposed method employs a data-driven framework to identify and model latent patterns in log data through a stochastic representation of a high-dimensional, non-parametric reservoir classifier. By leveraging the probabilistic nature of this model, the system can automatically detect formations and estimate associated uncertainties. Furthermore, the study examines how various factors influence the resulting classification. A field case demonstrates the practical application of this technique for real-time well control decisions.

Named entity recognition (NER) has long been a pivotal task in natural language processing, with nested NER emerging as a significant extension. Existing research predominantly relies on heuristic conversion methods to transform nested structures into linear formats, processing them via standard NLP pipelines. However, this study proposes a fundamental paradigm shift by treating natural language as holistic tree-like data and implementing a holistic nested NLP pipeline. Our approach introduces a novel neural sequence-to-tree architecture designed to process both the input sentences and output parsed entities simultaneously in their original hierarchical forms. Experiments conducted on two benchmark datasets demonstrate that this new method achieves state-of-the-art performance.

This study examines localization within wireless sensor networks, specifically addressing how to determine the positions of nodes in an environment where multiple wireless technologies coexist. Such settings often lead to significant disruptions in ranging measurements caused by interferences between technologies, a factor frequently overlooked in current research. The analysis considers a scenario where a primary positioning technology is compromised by the presence of secondary technologies. The paper establishes that localization remains feasible even when ranging data is corrupted by these intrusions, provided the spatial deployment of sensors adheres to specific structural constraints. Furthermore, it characterizes these necessary positioning conditions and characterizes the resulting location estimation bias introduced by the interference.

Social media users increasingly favor code-switching and code-mixing over using a single language, creating a strong demand for NL tools that cater to these multilingual groups. However, developing such tools is difficult because these communities are often linguistically diverse and geographically dispersed, making it hard to gather sufficient data for effective model training. Furthermore, the dynamic nature of mixing different languages introduces significant complexity. This paper examines the various factors and hurdles involved in creating natural language processing tools for code-mixed environments. It also proposes a comprehensive framework designed to support the entire lifecycle of developing these multilingual NLP utilities.

Assessing automatic image description methods is challenging, particularly when few human references are available. This study investigates strategies for evaluating these descriptions without abundant human-generated references. We introduce a method that leverages partial references from individual users to evaluate predictions, utilizing a learned relevance model to identify the most pertinent descriptions from existing references. This approach was tested on two datasets: one containing human references for specific subsets of images, and another with descriptions generated by a description task. Results indicate that this method significantly outperforms current state-of-the-art techniques.

Tantalum oxide crystals ($Ta_2O_5$) are renowned for their exceptional dielectric breakdown strength, making them a leading contender for next-generation high-voltage power electronics. Theoretical models suggest that the fundamental base state of this material is a single base crystal structure, yet experimental efforts to isolate and characterize this phase have thus far been unsuccessful. This study presents a combined approach using Monte Carlo simulations and ab-initio methods to demonstrate that a metastable phase transition can reorganize the base state into the well-documented monoclinic $\delta-Ta_2O_5$ structure. Furthermore, the research indicates that the base state possesses a significantly higher theoretical breakdown strength than the $\delta$-phase, offering a promising pathway for future experiments to achieve the base state and validate the simulation results.

This study examines U.S. Reddit usage patterns to explore how misinformation spreads, utilizing extensive data from r/politics that covers the 2020 election cycle and the broader period analyzed encompasses user interactions, content visibility, and the specific function of the platform's alphabetical sorting feature. We found that users disproportionately engaged with inaccurate content regardless of alphabetical arrangement, yet the Big Geographic Sort (BGS) system significantly amplified this exposure by positioning such material at the top of feeds; specifically, users encountered misinformation 30% more frequently under BGS compared to standard chronological sorting. Consequently, the research highlights that BGS facilitates the widespread visibility of false narratives, potentially distorting users' perception of their prevalence and accuracy.

Analyzing information streams is essential for detecting anomalies that demand immediate attention. However, existing anomaly detection methods often require extensive data, which is unavailable during unexpected events. This study proposes an approach that identifies anomalies with minimal samples by leveraging the inherent structure of the data. We define the input data as a directed graph where nodes represent items and edges signify temporal relationships. An anomaly is characterized as a collection of nodes forming a subgraph that stands out from the background. We introduce a statistical model of the background data as a random graph process and derive a rejection region for anomaly detection. Our method offers a probabilistic guarantee that the probability of false alarms remains below a predetermined threshold $\alpha$. We validate our approach through simulations and experiments using Twitter data.

This study examines the acoustic characteristics of human teachers providing physical guidance for manipulation tasks to robotic systems. Recognizing that human collaboration relies on both visual and auditory inputs, there is a scarcity of data regarding the sounds instructors use to direct robot actions. We analyzed audio recordings from three separate experiments, focusing on teachers' vocal traits during demonstrations of a unidimensional sliding task. The analysis covered voice pitch (fundamental frequency), loudness (loudness), and pitch variability (jitter), as well as acoustic energy distribution across frequency ranges (spectral tilt). Results indicate that when human demonstrators offer physical assistance while instructing robots, their voices exhibit higher pitch, pitch fluctuation, and voice intensity, alongside altered spectral characteristics compared to non-contact demonstrations. These findings offer a basis for future research into the acoustic profiles of human teachers demonstrating physical skills to robots.

Non-linear features found in natural languages, such as the varying phrase structures within a sentence, can be effectively captured through language models utilizing recurrent neural networks guided by structured prior. To train these models, it is essential to convert syntactic trees into linear sequences via different traversal strategies, a process that currently relies on ad-hoc methods lacking a rigorous theoretical basis. This paper introduces a new algorithm for generating random binary trees that addresses this gap. The method guarantees uniform distribution across all possible shape outcomes and operates in linear time relative to the node count. Furthermore, the algorithm was generalized to support ordered trees with diverse arity. Empirical testing on binary and ordered trees up to 10,000 nodes confirms its efficiency, while experiments with structurally diverse natural language trees demonstrate that the generated traversal orders ensure uniformly distributed results.

Using a differential equation approach, we examine the large $N$ behavior of the two-dimensional $O(N)$-symmetric Euler-Arnard equations, which govern the classical states of $W$-conformal field theories. Our analysis reveals that these equations admit a distinct class of solutions where the two largest eigenvalues of the associated eigenvector matrix remain constant throughout time. We demonstrate a duality between this system and a specific Euler-Arnold equation defined on a Euclidean Heisenberg algebra, utilizing it to derive exact classical states for the related Euler-Arnold equation afffiliated with the $q$-deformed Heron-Yang (Yd) model. Furthermore, we establish a correspondence linking this ditional system to the critical $q$-deformed Heron-Yang (Yd) model. Finally, we compute the values of the central charge and Euler angles within the large $N$ limit.

Conversational AI is currently a rapidly expanding field, with new initiatives launching at an accelerated pace. As the number of chatbots increases, so does the necessity for rigorous quality assurance. However, automated testing methods available today often fail to adequately address the unique challenges inherent to these systems. To bridge this gap, we present MachineTest, a novel testing framework designed specifically for chatbots that facilitates testing interactions between a bot and a machine-controlled user agent. We evaluated the utility of this solution by applying it to test a prototype conversational agent, demonstrating how the system supports the efficient creation of test cases and ensures the viability of our approach.

The potential existence of a massive Planet X has been hypothesized for decades, yet its influence on the orbits of known planets remains difficult to detect. This study investigates the detectability of Planet X's gravitational effects by analyzing the orbital residuals of the eight major planets, accounting for the dynamical influence of the Kuiper Belt. We conclude that a 10 Earth-mass object near the heliosphere's edge would likely be identifiable through the semi-major axis orbital elements of the known planets. Specifically, we utilize the semi-major axes of the four outermost planets to constrain the Heliopause's location, a method that could reveal Planet X despite the uncertainty regarding the outer boundary of the solar system. Assuming Planet X resides beyond the orbits of the known planets, the 68% confidence interval for Planet X's mass is estimated between 4.5 and 14.5 solar masses, with a median value of approximately 10.8 solar masses. Furthermore, the median 68% confidence interval for Planet X's semi-major axis falls between 510 and 610 astronomical units, centering at roughly 580 units. The analysis indicates that the detectability of Planet X is significantly contingent upon the precision of the mass and dynamical models used for the major planets, as well as the specific dataset employed. We examine potential imprints on the Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB) sky resulting from singular "eons" situated between consecutive universes in Conformal Cyclic Cosmology. By analyzing the high-redshift universe's properties immediately prior to a Hogg transition and the resulting high-redshift objects, we predict the appearance of specific high-temperature sources in the CMB. These predictions are evaluated against data from the Planck mission, which shows no evidence of such anomalies. Furthermore, we explore the implications of this null detection for the Planck data and the potential signatures of other cosmological models.

Few-shot learning aims to generalize a classifier by training on classes with very limited labeled examples. A critical challenge in this domain is constructing effective decision boundaries that accommodate these scarce samples. To address this, we introduce a new method for learning class-level prototypes. This approach is designed to leverage the statistical properties of natural image distributions, positing that a prototype should reflect the typical characteristics of a class. Consequently, a natural decision boundary emerges by measuring the distance between a test image and these prototypes. We formalize this approach as an optimization problem solved via a straightforward algorithm. Experiments on the standard mini- and few-shot Instagram (mini-FSInstagram and few-FSInstagram) benchmarks demonstrate that these prototypes significantly improve few-shot classification accuracy.

In the realm of e-commerce, recommendation systems are pivotal for aiding user purchasing decisions and boosting sales. However, these systems face hurdles such as data sparsity and the challenge of cold starts. To address these issues, this paper introduces a Multi-Sparse-Domain Cooperative Recommendation (MS-DCR) framework. This model facilitates cross-domain recommendation by leveraging implicit information from multiple unrelated domains. Specifically, it employs an implicit comprehensive attribute preference learning approach to capture hidden user preferences through various indirect signals. Furthermore, the model utilizes implicit information from several independent domains to generate recommendations for a target domain characterized by sparsity. A key innovation of the model is its ability to process user attributes in a sparse, sequential manner, which enhances the efficiency of online implicit attribute recognition. Extensive experiments conducted on two real-world datasets confirm the model's superiority over existing state-of-the-art methods.

Automated quality assurance (QA) methods are increasingly utilized to detect artifacts in MRI scans, yet current deep learning-based approaches often underperform in clinical environments. We posit that the primary cause of this underperformance lies in a lack of robustness regarding distributional shifts. To investigate this, we conducted a comprehensive analysis of the factors influencing QA models by varying acquisition parameters, such as field strength, coil configurations, and patient demographics, across 14,000 MRI datasets. Our findings indicate that shifts in these specific factors induce significant changes in image statistics, whereas shifts in diagnostic labels have a comparatively minor impact. Furthermore, models trained on data from a single factor combination failed to generalize to test sets with different factors, resulting in a 20% drop in performance. Although incorporating data from multiple factor variations improved robustness, the models still failed to match the performance seen on the training factor, suggesting that current approaches do not adequately capture the complexity of these shifts. Finally, we demonstrate that the difficulty in generalization is exacerbated by the inherent imbalance of factor distributions in available real-world data.

The proliferation of privately owned electric vehicles (EVs) offers a pathway to decarbonize the transportation sector and bolster grid sustainability. Nevertheless, a mass EV adoption could also introduce novel vulnerabilities to the power infrastructure. This study examines the impact of private EVs on distribution network resilience by analyzing how such vehicles influence the network's ability to withstand and recover from significant disturbances, specifically prolonged outages. To address this, a bi-level optimization framework is proposed. At the high level, the model simulates the strategic choices of EV drivers regarding charging timing and duration during grid availability. Concurrently, the low-level component represents the electrical power flow and calculates the charging loads imposed by EVs on the distribution system. By integrating these behavioral and physical layers, the approach evaluates both the charging behavior of EVs and the overall system state. Results indicate that, contrary to expectations, private EVs may occasionally enhance the network's capacity to cope with major disruptions. Furthermore, the proposed methodology is versatile, capable of accommodating various charging preferences and vehicle ownership structures.

Inspired by the drive theory from economics, this study proposes a new Multi-Agent Recurrent Meeting (MARW) framework for scheduling meetings among distributed agents. Within this model, agents autonomously select meeting times based on their individual preference signals, which represent the duration until they desire to convene again. The proposed system incorporates a recurrence mechanism ensuring agents return to meetings within a defined timeframe. Analysis of this dynamic system identifies a sufficient condition for guaranteeing recurrent meetings and defines the optimal meeting time via a social cost function. Furthermore, the work examines how varying signal strengths influence the convergence rate toward the optimal time. Numerical simulations validate the proposed theoretical findings.

This study explores the structural, electronic, and magnetic properties of GdSn$_3$, CmSn$_3$, and the solid solution Gd$_x$Cm$_{1-x}$Sn$_3$ compounds using first-principles methods. The investigation begins with a detailed analysis of the pure GdSn$_3$ and CmSn$_3$ phases. Subsequently, the formation of the Gd$_x$Cm$_{1-x}$Sn$_3$ alloy is examined by constructing a supercell containing a single Gd atom substituted into a Cm lattice, as well as cells with three Gd atoms replacing Cm. The results indicate that GdSn$_3$ and CmSn$_3$ are stable in the AuCu$_3$L1$_2$ structure type, with the supercell configurations demonstrating negative formation energies, confirming the thermodynamic stability of the resulting superstructure and alloy. While both pure compounds exhibit non-magnetic stability in their ground states, the supercell configurations are stabilized when Gd and Cm carry magnetic moments. Band structure analysis reveals these materials to be metallic, with the supercells showing a minor increase in the band gap compared to their constituent elements. The calculated formation energies suggest the alloy can be produced via a substitutional mechanism. Finally, the emergence of magnetism in the superstructure and alloy is attributed to the formation of localized magnetic moments on the rare-earth ions.

We utilize the baryon-to-photon ratio from the Planck mission to forecast the abundances of exotic baryons and the total counts of all exotic particles. The calculations indicate that the Planck data supports a scenario in which the universe is composed of 100% exotic matter. Within this framework, the collective abundance of such matter is constrained by the ratio of the proton mass to the electron mass. Consequently, the total number of exotic particles is predicted to be approximately $10^{86}$.

We establish a foundation theorem for irreducible irreducible B-type Coxeter groups that serves as a generalized version of the well-established result for A-type groups. In its proof, we establish several auxiliary results with independent significance. The theorem itself provides an explicit parameterization of the positive roots, demonstrating that their complex reflection arrangement generates the braid group associated with a specific complex reflection group. In doing so, we also define a generator set for the associated braid group.

Gravitational lensing is a powerful probe of the cosmic web, yet it remains challenging to constrain due to the difficulty in mapping dark matter structures. While strong lensing events, characterized by significant magnification and multiple images, offer clear evidence of lensing, feeble lensing—producing subtle effects across large samples—is essential for achieving precise limits on matter clustering. This study presents the first comprehensive analysis of feeble lensing for a complete Type Ia supernova (SN Ia) dataset, utilizing the Pantheon sample. The analysis reveals that the resulting magnitudes and convergence fields contain substantial information regarding dark matter distribution. By leveraging the H0LiCOW sample of strong lensing systems to calibrate the analysis, we developed a methodology to reconstruct the matter power spectrum from feeble lensing signals. Our reconstructed power spectrum aligns well with results from weak lensing surveys and cosmic shear studies. Furthermore, the analysis indicates that combining feeble lensing signals from numerous SNe Ia yields a matter density ($\Omega_{m}$) constraint with approximately 10% precision, while the associated lensing probability distribution function offers a further 15% improvement over models that do not incorporate feeble lensing data.

This note introduces the fundamentals of SPDEs, beginning with the introduction of Wiener space and the associated Fubini-Nietschard theorem, before progressing to the definition of Itô integrals and the fundamental lemma of stochastic analysis. It then examines the classical heat equation and its stochastic counterpart, the stochastic heat equation, concluding with an overview of the noisy Burger's equation along with the core concepts required to formulate the theory of SPDEs.

Hubs constitute a compact, high-bandwidth, and cost-effective alternative to fiber optic couplers. This study presents the design and experimental verification of 1x3 hubs fabricated in silicon-on-insulator technology. These 1x3 hubs were created by merging two 1x2 hubs, resulting in a lower insertion loss of 4.6 dB and a crosstalk level of -18.6 dB when compared to their respective 1x2 counterparts. Additionally, the device demonstrates superior performance regarding polarization independence and thermal stability.

An MRI image represents a two-dimensional intensity plot where axes correspond to a cross-section of the human body and values indicate pixel brightness. Since an MRI scan covers the entire body as a series of 2D slices, an MRI image, in the common usage of this study, refers to a single 2D image representing one such slice. The research presented here examines various image analysis techniques designed to identify tumors within an MRI image, with the goal of automating the diagnostic process and reducing reliance on manual inspection by medical professionals.

The paper begins by outlining fundamental image analysis concepts, including image filtering, convolution, and the Laplacian operator. It subsequently details specific methods for image segmentation, covering thresholding, region growing, and active contours (also known as snakes). Finally, the authors outline an automatic tumor detection algorithm grounded in these principles and provides a performance evaluation of the proposed approach.

We present a fresh derivation of a well-known result by S. M. Germain, which describes a specific algebraic mechanism for degrading non-zero polynomials in $\mathbb{Q}[X]$ to demonstrate the divisibility of Bernoulli numbers $B_{2n}$ into $2n$. This process is illustrated through several cases, including finding the precise power with which $p-1$ divides $B_{\alpha(p-1)-2}$ for any $\alpha \in \mathbb{Q}$ and prime $p$, where previously only an existence proof existed. The approach relies on the observation that the logarithmic derivative of the $\lambda$-adic zeta function, $\frac{\lambda(s)}{z\lambda(s)}$, serves as a polynomial in $\lambda$ involving coefficients tied to z\lambda coefficients and coefficients of Chebyshev polynomials of the second kind.

Stellar activity noise poses a significant challenge in the search for exoplanets, often mimicking or obscuring the signals of planetary companions. This study evaluates a selection and weighting scheme for spectral line features used in least-squares deconvolution (LSD), a technique that enhances the signal-to-noise ratio of the radial velocity signal by integrating information from thousands of lines. The proposed approach randomly chooses a subset of features and assigns weights inversely proportional to their individual noise levels. This method is contrasted with a parametric model that selects specific lines based on physical parameters such as equivalent width and wavelength. Applied to the active star AD Leo within a mock dataset, the proposed randomized approach yielded a line-of-sight velocity signal approximately 10% stronger than that produced by the parametric model.

This paper examines the design of a two-tier hierarchical scope sectoring system tailored for on-demand sensor domains. It introduces the architecture, protocols, and algorithms governing sensor behavior within limited, temporary regions. A key feature of this design is the introduction of the Bidirectional Link Caliber (BLC) mechanism, which operates independently of hardware. BLC dynamically evaluates network links to optimize data transmission rates. The research also analyzes the system's energy efficiency and compares it against existing protocols for mobile sinks, concluding that this approach offers a more energy-efficient solution for creating transient domains.

We introduce a method for evaluating contextual information, which is often utilized by deep-based object recognizers to fill performance gaps. Our approach involves analyzing the statistical interrelationships between contextual features and feature vectors of objects. Our analysis reveals that the strong performance of deep-based recognizers stems from the fact that their extracted features implicitly encode these statistical dependencies. We introduce a new feature engineering technique that explicitly incorporates this information to enhance DeepLab performance on the Pascal VOC 2012 validation set for deep object recognition.

This research investigates a specific Kirchhoff type elliptic system defined on a bounded domain within $\mathbb{R}^2$, characterized by singularity and expanding under Trudinger conditions. The primary objective is to demonstrate the system's existence of a doubly grounded solution.
